findings.evidence: plot.py draws head at zorder 3 with markersize 5 and then, for base, an extra scatter at s=45 with zorder 4, which paints over the head line and marker. Measured on image-0.png in the booking panel's plateau band (render rows 140-160, columns 990-1260): 3784 pure-white pixels, 53 of them directly beside a grey edge pixel, i.e. the base squares' white interiors sit on top of the head trace.
findings.summary: The base series is redrawn as a large white-faced square in a separate scatter above the head line, so wherever the two arms coincide the head marker and the head line beneath it are painted out and the reader sees a white-centred grey square with the blue line interrupted at its edge. The head arm is the one the figure reports on, and it is the one that disappears exactly where the arms agree, which is the figure's headline. It stays non-blocking because the blue line enters and leaves each square at the same height, so the head level at every occluded iterate remains readable, and the interruption itself shows where base sits on head; the caption also states that the overlap is the result. A reader who had not read the caption could, however, mistake the broken blue line for missing head data at those iterates, and no filled blue circle appears anywhere in the four panels.

findings.evidence: plot.py computes lower and upper as floored and ceiled decades of the plotted values and then calls set_ylim(10**(lower-0.3), 10**(upper+0.3)), a fixed 1.6-decade window whenever the data occupy one decade or less. Measured on image-0.png over plot areas about 213 rows tall: blue curve rows 184-278 in 'full' (94 rows, 0.44 of the panel), 148-292 in 'booking' (144 rows, 0.68), 460-569 in 'geometry' (109 rows, 0.51) and 498-541 in 'flux' (43 rows, 0.20).
findings.summary: Every panel gets the same axis construction: snap the limits to whole decades of the data and then pad by 0.3 decades on each side. The pad is fixed, so a panel whose data span less than a decade is zoomed out far more than one whose data span several. The flux panel spans about 0.3 decades and so uses about 20 percent of its height for its variation, against 44 to 68 percent in the full, booking and geometry panels, which makes the flux error read as flatter and steadier than the other blocks at a glance. It stays non-blocking because the decade labels are present and legible, so a reader who reads the axis is not misled by the compression.

rubric_lines: RUBRIC legibility: pass. Four log-y panels in a 2x2 grid, one per residual block, each naming its quantity on the y axis ('full relative error', 'booking relative error', 'geometry relative error', 'flux relative error'), a shared x axis 'accepted iterate' labelled 0-9 on the bottom row, and one unframed two-entry legend above the panels. Every axis label, tick label and legend entry is legible at native resolution and both arms are followable across all ten iterates. Two reading costs are recorded as non-blocking findings: in one panel (booking) the arms differ by far less than a pixel at this log scale and the reader sees one trace, and in every panel the head marker is painted out under the base marker (finding 1).

RUBRIC data_ink: pass. Two line-and-marker series per panel and nothing else inside the axes apart from the log ticks that make the values readable. Measured on the render with a tight colour tolerance: 6957 px of head blue #2865b2 and 9750 px of base grey #929292 across the whole canvas, with no shaded region, band, area fill or gradient inside any axes.

RUBRIC decoration: pass. Top and right spines are absent on every panel (only the bottom spines at render rows 342 and 625-626 and the left spines at columns 223-224 and 795-796 are drawn), no gridline is drawn, and there is no background fill, panel frame or drop shadow. The y tick ladder is thinned to at most about five labelled decades per panel.

RUBRIC contrast: pass. All axis, tick and legend text is near-black on white. Head blue #2865b2 is about 5.8:1 on white; base grey #929292 is about 3.1:1, at the 3:1 graphics floor, and the arms are separated by marker shape (white-faced square against a line) in addition to hue.

RUBRIC table_form: pass. Ten accepted iterates against four error blocks with two arms overlaid is a trend comparison, which a line plot shows and a table does not; the exact six-spacing ladder is tabled in the evidence fragment, so the image carries only the shape the table cannot give at a glance.

RUBRIC label_collision: pass. No text is clipped and no label overlaps another label or the data. The render's ink bounding box is rows 3-685 and columns 137-1372; the outer 4-px frames carry zero non-white pixels on the left, right and bottom and 40 on the top, all of them the tops of the legend glyphs at rows 3-7. The legend clears the canvas top edge by three rows: not clipped, but it is the tightest margin in the layout, and the drawing script's own refusal check (plot.py check_text) is what keeps it from crossing.
